findings.title: Selected-route coherence is absent from the pure lease interface
findings.diagnosis: Plan-to-contract route and declared-permission ceilings now work. The requested remaining F01 check is not implementable at DeriveLease: no input supplies the selected route identity, resolved route permissions, or an approval-bound projection of that route. The core approval carries an opaque transition digest; DeriveLease never resolves its route payload. Therefore D2 cannot establish that selected route == approved plan route, or that selected route permissions fit the grant, before reporting an active lease. This is an observed interface/validation gap and a mandatory closure failure. It is not a reproduced unauthorized dispatch. Launch admission remains D3–D6 scope.

evidence.observation: LeaseRequest has no selected/approved route projection. DeriveLease compares route labels in plan with contract labels, then copies plan ImplementerRoute into Lease. It does not compare a selected profile or its permissions with the plan grant. Core route binding exposes an opaque transition digest, not the route payload.
The supplied closure criterion explicitly requires permission broadening and approved route identity mismatch to refuse before the lease becomes active.
Out-of-contract plan labels and read_only -> bounded_write plan broadening refuse. These controls test declarations only, not the selected route.

fix.action: Define route strings as stable identities and extend the pure request with a trusted host projection of the selected route plus its approval-bound identity/permission grant. Verify that the projection references the active core route approval and matches the selected plan unit; compare resolved permissions with both unit and contract ceilings before ReasonNone. Refuse an absent projection for contract-backed leases. Preserve legal Independent validation correction issuers by retaining the preceding valid route binding.
fix.why: The comparison needs both sides: the approved plan declaration and the route actually selected under a core approval. The current request has only the first side.

verification.method: Keep contract, plan bytes and accepted_plan_digest fixed. Supply matching selected profile and approval as a positive control. Then vary profile identity, permission class, approval reference and unit independently.
verification.expected: Matching selection succeeds. Each mismatch and missing projection refuses before the lease is active.

verification.method: Use a selected bounded_write route under a read_only unit/contract, then restore read_only; include legal Independent validation -> Implementation authorization rework.
verification.expected: Broadening refuses. Matching read_only and legal rework succeed with the proper route binding.

verification.method: Rerun existing full test/vet/race and independent lease/rewind/legacy-byte controls.
verification.expected: All pass; no illegal issuer, scope widening or legacy serialization change.

fix.tradeoffs: A required route projection changes callers of the new D2 API and needs an explicit identity convention. It must not add another authority source or treat host telemetry as human approval. This remedy is proposed; no implementation was made.
fix.alternative: Keep DeriveLease explicitly as a route-scoped grant and move selected-route admission to a separate deterministic API. That can be sound only after the human authoritatively amends the present F01 before-active closure criterion; the auditor cannot waive it.

limitations: Fresh audit context contains the user dispatch and allowed neutral closure criteria. No implementer narrative or prior audit verdict was read before this freeze. Code comments and author-written tests were inspected as artifacts, not accepted as proof.

Isolation is a separate fresh auditor context and a filesystem copy. It is not a separate VM or container trust boundary. The OS, host-managed chain and caller-provided current policy/counters are trusted, as scoped.

Only D1 and pure D2 are evaluated. No operational admission, reservation accounting, reconciliation, criterion credit, finding disposition, architecture amendment, release or full Gate D completion is certified.
The F01 selected-route mismatch is an observed API gap. No valid runtime mismatch test can be passed into the current request type. No unauthorized launch is claimed.

Pure dependency and counter tests use independently authored synthetic records. Six whole-run rewind scenarios also traverse the real Apply/store path with fresh approvals. Real Apply tests reuse existing low-level Git fixture and approval-construction helpers; acceptance assertions and test sequences are auditor-authored.

Initial full normal/race runs failed the scratch-store location assertion because the copy was under /tmp. A second environment placed GOTMPDIR outside TMPDIR and failed scratch positive controls. Final runs set both to <output>/runtime, outside the worktree, and passed. All failed logs are retained.
No Jev decision tool is available. Auditor judgments use the documented direct fallback. No worker/model API or nested agent was dispatched.
Go toolchain is go1.27.1 linux/amd64; module declares go 1.21. No other Go version or platform was tested.

The repository was read-only by audit conduct and sandbox protection of Git internals, not mounted as an immutable snapshot. Start/end HEAD, status, binary diff digest and every untracked hash match; this does not prove no transient concurrent change occurred. The tested copied target bytes also match the source manifest.

Displayed tool output was sometimes truncated. Complete test logs, the copied source and the independently authored test files remain in the output directory. An initial auditor fixture draft had a syntax error; it was corrected before acceptance runs. No product finding relies on that draft failure.
